proposals.before: Then there were exemplars such as the wife of Liang Hong, who shared her husband's seclusion without complaint, and Gong Jiang, who swore never to enter a second household—models of wifely duty and maternal virtue celebrated in the histories; these represent an even higher standard.
proposals.after: Then there were exemplars such as the wife of Liang Hong, who shared her husband's seclusion without complaint, and Gong Jiang, who swore never to enter a second household—models of wifely duty and maternal virtue celebrated in the histories; these too are among their strengths.
proposals.reason: Chinese 其次…又其長也 ranks these as the next exemplary type after the martyrs, not a higher standard than they.

proposals.before: Pei Shi, wife of Li Dewu—Pei Shi, styled Shuying, was the daughter of Pei Ju, Director of the Household Ministry and Duke of Anyi.
proposals.after: Pei Shi, wife of Li Dewu, was styled Shuying and was the daughter of Pei Ju, Director of the Household Ministry and Duke of Anyi.
proposals.reason: Literal English repeats Pei Shi after the em dash, duplicating the subject already named.

proposals.before: She married Li Dewu, but after only a year he was banished to Lingnan because of his cousin Jin Cai's case.
proposals.after: She married Li Dewu, but after only a year he was banished to Lingnan because of his paternal uncle Jin Cai's case.
proposals.reason: 從父 denotes a paternal uncle, not a cousin.

proposals.before: When the Taizong besieged Luoyang, Qing plotted to turn against Shichong and wished to come over to the Tang together with his wife.
proposals.after: When Taizong besieged Luoyang, Qing plotted to turn against Shichong and wished to come over to the Tang together with his wife.
proposals.reason: English article before the temple name Taizong is ungrammatical.

proposals.before: Li Shi, wife of Yang San'an—Li Shi was a native of Jingyang in Yongzhou.
proposals.after: Li Shi, wife of Yang San'an, was a native of Jingyang in Yongzhou.
proposals.reason: The literal English repeats the subject after an em dash, producing a fused apposition not present as a second clause in the Chinese.

proposals.before: By day Li worked the fields; by night she spun and wove; within several years she buried her parents-in-law and seven of her husband's uncles, nephews, and brothers—deeply admired near and far.
proposals.after: By day Li worked the fields; by night she spun and wove; within several years she conducted seven funerals for her parents-in-law and her husband's uncles, nephews, and brothers—deeply admired near and far.
proposals.reason: 七喪 is the total count of funerals, not seven relatives in addition to the parents-in-law.

proposals.before: Wang Shi, wife of Wei Heng—Wang Shi was a native of Qi in Zizhou.
proposals.after: Wang Shi, wife of Wei Heng, was a native of Qi in Zizhou.
proposals.reason: The em-dash restatement doubles the subject and is not a second Chinese clause.

proposals.before: Jing Shi, mother of Fan Huiren—Jing Shi, styled Xiangzi, was a native of Hedong in Puzhou.
proposals.after: Jing Shi, mother of Fan Huiren, styled Xiangzi, was a native of Hedong in Puzhou.
proposals.reason: The em-dash restates Jing Shi unnecessarily; Chinese is a single identification plus courtesy name and native place.

proposals.before: At the slightest hint of persuasion she would weep in grief and resentment; this happened four times.
proposals.after: At the slightest hint of persuasion she would weep in grief and resentment; this happened again and again.
proposals.reason: 數四 here means repeatedly, not a count of exactly four occasions.

proposals.before: The Filial Daughter Jia of Puzhou—the Filial Daughter Jia was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.
proposals.after: The Filial Daughter Jia of Puzhou was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.
proposals.reason: The Chinese dittography 孝女賈氏孝女賈氏 should not be reproduced as two English subjects.

proposals.before: Lu Shi, wife of Zheng Yizong—Lu Shi was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou, daughter of Lu Yanheng.
proposals.after: Lu Shi, wife of Zheng Yizong, was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou and daughter of Lu Yanheng.
proposals.reason: The em-dash restatement doubles Lu Shi; Chinese is one identification.

proposals.before: At eighteen Shangguan married Prince Lingui, succeeding as consort after the lamented King of Chu.
proposals.after: At eighteen Shangguan married Prince Lingui, succeeding in the line of King Ai of Chu.
proposals.reason: 哀王 is the posthumous title Ai, not the adjective lamented; 繼楚哀王後 marks succession in King Ai of Chu's line.

proposals.before: She married the Duke of Yanshou, son of Qinming, to Minzhi.
proposals.after: She married Minzhi, son of Qinming, Duke of Yanshou.
proposals.reason: 適延壽公於欽明子敏直 means she married Minzhi, son of the Duke of Yanshou Yu Qinming; the literal English reverses the spouse.

proposals.before: Xi Shi, wife of Zou Baoying—Xi Shi; her place of origin is unknown.
proposals.after: Xi Shi, wife of Zou Baoying; her place of origin is unknown.
proposals.reason: Literal English repeats Xi Shi after an em dash, duplicating the subject already named.

proposals.before: Wei Shi, wife of Song Tingyu—Wei Shi was a native of Gucheng in Dingzhou, descendant of the Sui Authoring Gentleman Yanquan.
proposals.after: Wei Shi, wife of Song Tingyu, was a native of Gucheng in Dingzhou, descendant of the Sui Authoring Gentleman Yanquan.
proposals.reason: Literal English doubles the opening name-lemma splice rather than naming a second person.

proposals.before: Her father Xian enjoyed a fine reputation; during Wu Zetian's reign he served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace and Left Assistant of the Ministry of Works.
proposals.after: Her father Xian enjoyed a fine reputation; during Wu Zetian's reign he served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace and Left Assistant of the Wenchang (Department of State Affairs).
proposals.reason: Wenchang Left Assistant is the Zhou title for Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, not the Ministry of Works.

proposals.before: Her father Xian had a fine reputation; during Wu Zetian's reign he served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace and Left Assistant of the Ministry of Works.
proposals.after: Her father Xian had a fine reputation; during Wu Zetian's reign he served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace and Left Assistant of the Wenchang (Department of State Affairs).
proposals.reason: Same office error as the idiomatic line: 文昌左丞 is not the Ministry of Works.

proposals.before: On the eve of the wedding they were about to tell Lu;
proposals.after: Only on the eve of the wedding did they tell Lu;
proposals.reason: Chinese 方以告盧 means they informed her then, not that they were merely about to tell her.

proposals.before: Jingzhao Assistant Cao Luhai composed a rhapsody in their praise.
proposals.after: Jingzhao Prefect Cao Luhai composed a rhapsody in their praise.
proposals.reason: 京兆尹 is Jingzhao Prefect (Yin), not Assistant.

proposals.before: Jingzhao Assistant Cao Luhai composed a rhapsody to praise them.
proposals.after: Jingzhao Prefect Cao Luhai composed a rhapsody to praise them.
proposals.reason: 京兆尹 is Jingzhao Prefect, not Assistant.

proposals.before: At the time Cao Sheng was promoted to Prefect of Xuzhou; learning the bandits had surrendered, he led troops in a surprise attack.
proposals.after: At the time Cao Sheng served as Prefect of Xuzhou; learning the bandits had surrendered, he led troops in a surprise attack.
proposals.reason: 任 marks holding the office, not a promotion.

proposals.before: An edict said, "Li Shi, late wife of Lu Fu, Magistrate of Yuanwu in Zheng Prefecture, and Pei Shi, late wife of Wang Fan, Magistrate of Weishi in Bian Prefecture, and the like—exemplary conduct in their families, gentle clarity in their natures;
proposals.after: An edict said, "Li Shi, late wife of Lu Fu, Assistant Magistrate of Yuanwu in Zheng Prefecture, and Pei Shi, late wife of Wang Fan, Assistant Magistrate of Weishi in Bian Prefecture, and the like—exemplary conduct in their families, gentle clarity in their natures;
proposals.reason: 縣尉 is the county defender/assistant magistrate, not the magistrate (令); the same office is rendered Assistant Magistrate for 縣尉 later in the chunk.

proposals.before: His wife was then bound to a tree by the rebels, cut apart, and eaten; to the end she called to her husband, "Serve Vice Censor Wu well."
proposals.after: His wife was then bound to a tree by the rebels, cut apart, and eaten; to the end she called to her husband, "Serve Pushe Wu well."
proposals.reason: 烏僕射 is Pushe (Vice Director), not Vice Censor (御史).

proposals.before: Changling often served as Chief Administrator of Si Prefecture and his family had dwelt in Cai for generations.
proposals.after: Changling had been Chief Administrator of Si Prefecture and his family had dwelt in Cai for generations.
proposals.reason: 常為 marks a prior posting, not habitual often served.

proposals.before: He served Wu Shaocheng and Shaoyang in succession; by Yuanji's time he was Magistrate of Wu Fang.
proposals.after: He served Wu Shaocheng and Shaoyang in succession; by Yuanji's time he was Magistrate of Wufang.
proposals.reason: 吳房 is the county Wufang, not two words Wu Fang.

proposals.before: Xianzong heard with joy and urgently summoned Changling to court, directly appointing him Magistrate of Yancheng and Acting Investigating Censor, and granting the scarlet robe and fish tally.
proposals.after: Xianzong heard with joy and urgently summoned Changling to court, directly appointing him Magistrate of Yancheng and concurrent Investigating Censor, and granting the scarlet robe and fish tally.
proposals.reason: 兼 is concurrent tenure; 攝 is the acting tenure used later for Wei Yong.

proposals.before: When Zhang Hongjing governed Youzhou, he memorialized and appointed Yong Observation Aide, acting as Investigating Censor.
proposals.after: When Zhang Hongjing governed Youzhou, he memorialized and appointed him Observation Aide, acting as Investigating Censor.
proposals.reason: Yong Observation Aide fuses the personal name Yong with the office 觀察判官.

proposals.before: Fanghou, in the Taihe era served as Recorder of Yong Regional Commandery; he was falsely accused and killed by Pacification Commissioner Dong Changling.
proposals.after: Fanghou, in the Taihe era served as Recorder of the Yongzhou Area Command; he was falsely accused and killed by Pacification Commissioner Dong Changling.
proposals.reason: 邕州都督府 is the Yongzhou (邕) area command, not Yong in the sense of 永.

proposals.before: Now escorting four coffins, they have reached an inn in Chang'an Prefecture; the location of the late Prince of Yue's tomb is unknown—I beg the court's grace to grant my petition and permit return to the ancestral tomb.
proposals.after: Now escorting four coffins, they have reached an inn at Changle for temporary lodging; the location of the late Prince of Yue's tomb is unknown—I beg the court's grace to grant my petition and permit return to the ancestral tomb.
proposals.reason: 長樂旅店 is an inn at Changle, not an inn identified as Chang'an Prefecture.

proposals.before: Now escorting four coffins, they have reached Chang'an Prefecture's inn for temporary lodging; the location of the late Prince of Yue's tomb is not yet known—I beg Heaven's grace to grant my petition and permit return to the great tomb.
proposals.after: Now escorting four coffins, they have reached a Changle inn for temporary lodging; the location of the late Prince of Yue's tomb is not yet known—I beg Heaven's grace to grant my petition and permit return to the great tomb.
proposals.reason: 長樂 names Changle, not the Jingzhao/Chang'an prefectural office.

decisions.reason: 其次 introduces a second exemplary type after the martyrs, and 又其長也 marks these as a further excellence, not a higher standard than death-defying loyalty.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其次梁鴻之妻……又其長也。

decisions.reason: The Chinese names 裴氏 once, then 字淑英 and her father; the em-dash restatement invents a second Pei Shi not present in the source.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 李德武妻裴氏，字淑英，戶部尚書、安邑公矩之女也。

decisions.reason: 從父 is a paternal uncle, so 坐從父金才事 cannot be rendered as cousin Jin Cai's case.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 德武坐從父金才事徙嶺表

decisions.reason: 太宗 is the temple name Taizong; the English article in “the Taizong” is ungrammatical and is not licensed by the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 及太宗攻圍洛陽

decisions.reason: 楊三安妻李氏 is a single identification followed by native place; the em-dash repeats Li Shi as if a second clause.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 楊三安妻李氏，雍州涇陽人也。

decisions.reason: 者七喪 totals seven funerals covering 舅姑 and 夫之叔侄兄弟, not seven extra agnates besides the parents-in-law.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 葬舅姑及夫之叔侄兄弟者七喪

decisions.reason: 魏衡妻王氏 is named once before the native-place clause; the em-dash restatement doubles Wang Shi.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 魏衡妻王氏，梓州郪人也。

decisions.after: Jing Shi, mother of Fan Huiren, was styled Xiangzi and was a native of Hedong in Puzhou.
decisions.reason: The duplicated Jing Shi should be removed, but “mother of Fan Huiren, styled Xiangzi” can attach 字像子 to the son; the courtesy name belongs to 敬氏.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 樊會仁母敬氏，字像子，蒲州河東人也。

decisions.reason: 如此者數四 is an iterative “again and again,” not a count of exactly four occasions.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 如此者數四

decisions.reason: The chapter lemma repeats 孝女賈氏, but received editions identify one woman; English should not treat the splice as two subjects.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 孝女賈氏，濮州鄄城人也。

decisions.reason: 鄭義宗妻盧氏 is one subject of native place and parentage; the em-dash restatement doubles Lu Shi.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 鄭義宗妻盧氏，幽州范陽人，盧彥衡之女也。

decisions.after: At eighteen Shangguan married Prince Lingui, who succeeded in the line of King Ai of Chu.
decisions.reason: 哀王 is the posthumous title Ai, not “lamented,” but the proposed participle still makes Shangguan the successor; 繼楚哀王後 describes 靈龜’s succession.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 上官年十八，歸於靈龜，繼楚哀王後。

decisions.reason: 適延壽公於欽明子敏直 means she married Minzhi, son of Yu Qinming, Duke of Yanshou; the original reverses the spouse.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 適延壽公於欽明子敏直。

decisions.reason: 奚氏 is named once before 不知何許人也; the em-dash repeats Xi Shi without a second Chinese clause.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 鄒保英妻奚氏，不知何許人也。

decisions.reason: The lemma splice repeats 宋庭瑜妻魏氏, but the biography is one identification plus native place and ancestry, not two persons.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 宋庭瑜妻魏氏宋庭瑜妻魏氏，定州鼓城人，隋著作郎彥泉之後也。

decisions.reason: 文昌左丞 is the Zhou title for Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs (Wenchang), not the Ministry of Works.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 則天時歷鸞臺侍郎、文昌左丞

decisions.reason: The same office error appears in the literal line: 文昌左丞 is Wenchang Left Assistant, not Ministry of Works.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 則天時歷鸞臺侍郎、文昌左丞

decisions.reason: 方以告盧 marks the moment they did tell her, not that they were still about to tell her.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 將婚之夕，方以告盧

decisions.reason: 京兆尹 is Jingzhao Prefect (Yin), the same office already rendered Prefect for 第五琦, not Assistant.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 京兆尹曹陸海著賦以美之。

decisions.reason: 京兆尹 is Jingzhao Prefect, not Assistant, in the literal line as well.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 京兆尹曹陸海著賦以美之。

decisions.reason: 任徐州刺史 records tenure in office, not a promotion.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時曹升任徐州刺史

decisions.reason: 縣尉 is the county defender/assistant magistrate, distinct from 令; both Lu Fu and Wang Fan are 尉, not magistrates.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 鄭州原武縣尉盧甫亡妻李氏、汴州尉氏縣尉王泛亡妻裴氏

decisions.reason: 烏僕射 addresses Wu as Pushe (Vice Director), not Vice Censor (御史).

sourceWitness.excerpt: 善事烏僕射

decisions.reason: 常為泗州長史 marks a prior posting (常/嘗), not habitual “often served.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 昌齡常為泗州長史

decisions.reason: 吳房 is the county name Wufang, not two words Wu Fang.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 為吳房令

decisions.reason: 兼監察御史 is concurrent tenure; 攝 would be acting, as later for Wei Yong.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 直授郾城令、兼監察御史

decisions.reason: 奏授觀察判官 appoints him Observation Aide; “Yong Observation Aide” fuses the personal name 雍 into the office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 奏授觀察判官，攝監察御史

decisions.reason: 邕州都督府 is the Yongzhou (邕) area-command headquarters, not Yong in the 永 sense.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 任邕州都督府錄事參軍

decisions.reason: 長樂旅店權下 is temporary lodging at a Changle inn, not an inn of Chang’an Prefecture.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 已到長樂旅店權下

decisions.reason: 長樂 names Changle; the literal “Chang’an Prefecture’s inn” misreads the place.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 已到長樂旅店權下

claimRevisions.reason: The English title Vice Censor was produced by mistranslating 僕射; the unit supports the title Pushe Wu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 烏僕射
